newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat trends further down in hedging game.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat trends further down in hedging game.

text.p: Australian wheat futures continued to fall on the Sydney Futures Exchange on Wednesday with the January and March contracts changing hands in moderate trading.
January fell A$3.00 to A$185.00 a tonne while March fell by A$3.50 to A$186.00. A total of 15 lots traded, most in the January contract.
Australian wheat futures were still tracking the offshore market, Colin Lethbridge of ANZ McCaughan Futures Ltd said.
The market still anticipated a slightly larger crop than the 18.8 million tonnes forecast by the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics, he said.
"I think it'll be closer to nineteen point something, perhaps the high 19s," he said.
Australia was not expected to do much until the U.S. market broke one way or another. "No-one knows which way it will be at the moment," he said.
Ten A$200.00 January call options traded at a A$5.00 premium on Wednesday, an end-user protecting the upside, he said.
"If this market does have a weather scare, which is entirely possible, it'll move up fairly swiftly," he said.
